title: The Chess Robot That Fooled Napoleon

scenes.notes: He built a chess robot that beat nearly every player, and before every game he opened it up to prove it was empty.

scenes.notes: You see, an inventor has just rolled a wooden cabinet into the Empress's palace in Vienna.

scenes.notes: On top sits a life-size wooden man in a turban, staring down at a chess board. The whole court laughs.

layers.markup: <svg viewBox="0 0 60 110" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g stroke="#1b1240" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="8" y="98" width="44" height="10" rx="5" fill="#d9b35c"/><rect x="21" y="48" width="18" height="52" rx="4" fill="#f4eee1"/><path d="M30 6 Q42 30 30 44 Q18 30 30 6 Z" fill="#f2b13b"/><path d="M30 22 Q35 32 30 40 Q25 32 30 22 Z" fill="#fff3c4" stroke="none"/></g></svg>

scenes.notes: So he opens the doors one by one and holds a candle behind them. Nothing but gears.

layers.markup: <svg viewBox="0 0 60 110" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g stroke="#1b1240" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"><rect x="8" y="98" width="44" height="10" rx="5" fill="#d9b35c"/><rect x="21" y="48" width="18" height="52" rx="4" fill="#f4eee1"/><path d="M30 6 Q42 30 30 44 Q18 30 30 6 Z" fill="#f2b13b"/><path d="M30 22 Q35 32 30 40 Q25 32 30 22 Z" fill="#fff3c4" stroke="none"/></g></svg>

scenes.notes: He winds a key. The gears start ticking, and the Turk lifts its arm.

scenes.notes: The first count brave enough to play it gets crushed. No one is laughing now.
For eighty years the Turk travels Europe and America. It even beats Benjamin Franklin.
And when Napoleon tries to cheat, it puts his piece right back. Twice. The third time, it sweeps every piece off the board.
Then a museum fire burns the Turk to ash, and its secret finally comes out.
A chess master folded into the cabinet. When each door opened, he slid his seat to the other side, behind fake gears.
Magnets under the board showed him every move, and a lever moved the Turk's hand. His candle smoke slipped out through the turban.
The robot that beat Napoleon was a man in a box, playing by candlelight.
